title: #169 item-2 re-test, variant B -- #164's variant-B contract (full eleven-node `.ic`, no `uic`) at 125 C / 50 mA
claim: One of four variants of #169's initial-condition screen at 125 C / 50 mA, which re-tests #81 item 2 (a reported second, stable, non-regulating equilibrium: tt -> VOUT 2.093 V, FB 1.114 V, N_FBB 1.048 V; ss -> 2.014 V; fs -> 2.199 V) after #164 showed the method it rested on -- a `tran ... uic` with only v(vout) constrained -- is unreliable at the far gentler 27 C / 1 mA corner. The four variants run ONE circuit (sim/dropout-vs-load's DUT, C_OUT and ideal 50 mA load, VIN held at the corner supply) and vary ONLY the initial condition: V = #81's own contract (`.ic v(vout)=1.8` only, `uic`); F = the same `uic` analysis with all eleven nodes #169 names seeded at their intended-branch values; B = #164's variant-B contract (the same full `.ic`, no `uic`: constrained `.op`, then released); C = cold start from all-zero with the EN edge and the load ramped on once the loop is up. If F/B/C all settle inside the regulating window with a realizable node set while V does not, item 2 is a method artifact; if F/B/C also settle at #81's ~2.0-2.2 V state with all four realizability slacks >= 0, item 2 is a real second equilibrium. THIS VARIANT (B) is #164's variant-B pattern at #81's corner: the full eleven-node `.ic` constrains the operating-point solve to the intended branch, and the transient is released from it (no `uic`). SUBSTANTIATES NO SPEC ROW: this is diagnostic evidence for design/README.md's "#169" section, kept in its own experiment slug for the same reason #164's screen was (sim/mc-ic-screen-a/-b/-d): measurements/build_characterization_report.py resolves a spec row's evidence from the lexicographically last record under the slug EVIDENCE_MAP maps it to, nothing maps to this slug, and a screen record must never be picked up as sim/dropout-vs-load's Dropout-row evidence. The vout_ss window is the ratified Output row's verbatim only so that 'regulating' has one fixed meaning across the four variants.
statistical_convention: N/A (corner-matrix diagnostic screen, not a distribution claim)
corners_note: Only 125 C is declared, on purpose: #169 re-tests one reported finding, and #81 item 2 was reported at 125 C / 50 mA only (#164 already characterized 27 C). All five process corners (#81 checked tt/ss/fs; ff/sf were then excluded for the #69-era thermal-shutdown false-trip that #69 has since closed) and three supplies: 3.60 V is #81 item 2's own VIN; 3.30 V / 3.63 V are the ratified supply axis's nominal and top points (2.97 V is left out -- nothing in #81 item 2 was reported there, and at 125 C the ideal 50 mA load leaves it the least headroom, which would confound a branch-selection question with a dropout one).

measurements.name: vout_ss
measurements.note: Settled VOUT, averaged over 2.5m-3m. Bounded by the ratified Output row's window (spec/target-spec.md "Output", 1.8 V +-2% = 1.764-1.836 V, issue #1 / DR-006) purely as the REGULATING-BRANCH TEST this screen needs: a value inside it is the intended equilibrium, and #81 item 2's second equilibrium (2.014-2.199 V over ss/tt/fs) is far outside it. This slug substantiates no spec row -- see the claim.

measurements.name: vout_tail_span
measurements.note: Peak-to-peak VOUT over the same 2.5m-3m window (unbounded, diagnostic): the settledness witness -- a small span means the averaged node set below is a settled state, not a snapshot of something still moving.

measurements.name: vin_ss
measurements.note: Settled V(VIN) -- the top of the realizability chain below (it is the ideal source, so it equals the corner's supply).

measurements.name: vout_800u
measurements.note: V(VOUT) at t = 800 us, the transient length #81 item 2 reported its settled values at.

measurements.name: fb_ss
measurements.note: Node dump (unbounded -- diagnostic, no limit and therefore no verdict): settled V(xldo.fb), averaged over 2.5m-3m. Why this node: the feedback divider's tap (a sky130_fd_pr__res_xhigh_po node): #81 item 2 reported 1.114 V at tt against 1.2 V on the regulating branch.

measurements.name: n_fbb_ss
measurements.note: Node dump (unbounded -- diagnostic, no limit and therefore no verdict): settled V(xldo.n_fbb), averaged over 2.5m-3m. Why this node: the divider's lower tap (res_xhigh_po): #81 item 2 reported 1.048 V at tt, giving the FB:N_FBB ~0.94:1 ratio a passive string of three equal legs cannot produce (it must be 2:1).

measurements.name: ea_out_ss
measurements.note: Node dump (unbounded -- diagnostic, no limit and therefore no verdict): settled V(xldo.ea_out), averaged over 2.5m-3m. Why this node: the error amp's output = the pass-device gate.

measurements.name: real_nfbb_ge_0
measurements.note: Realizability check (#169 Scope item 3), one link of 0 <= V(N_FBB) <= V(FB) <= V(VOUT) <= VIN: this is the slack of V(N_FBB) >= 0. FB and N_FBB are fed ONLY by VOUT through a passive three-leg res_xhigh_po string, so every realizable settled state has all four slacks >= 0; a negative slack means the settled 'state' is the solver's unconverged iterate (#81 item 1 / #164), not a circuit equilibrium (#81 item 2). The bound is that algebra, not a spec row.
